tasks.title: Bar chart: hours of sleep by age and gender
tasks.prompt:
The chart below shows the average number of hours that men and women in five age groups sleep each night in one country.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

visual.title: Average hours of sleep per night, by age group and gender
visual.note: Fictional data created for practice purposes.

examinerNotes: Overview should note: both genders sleep least in the 31–50 group and most as teenagers; women sleep more than men up to 30, men more from 31 onwards.
tasks.modelAnswer:
The bar chart compares the average amount of sleep that men and women in five age groups have each night in one country.

Overall, both men and women sleep the most when they are teenagers and the least between the ages of 31 and 50, after which the amount of sleep rises again. Women sleep slightly longer than men up to the age of 30, but from the age of 31 onwards the opposite is true.

Teenagers aged 13 to 18 sleep the longest, with girls averaging 7.9 hours a night and boys 7.6 hours. Among young adults aged 19 to 30, these figures fall to 7.3 hours for women and 7.0 hours for men. Sleep then reaches its lowest point in the 31 to 50 age group, at 6.6 hours for men and 6.5 hours for women, perhaps reflecting the pressures of work and family life.

In the older age groups, sleep time increases again, but more noticeably for men. Men aged 51 to 70 sleep for 6.8 hours, rising to 7.2 hours for those over 70. Women's sleep increases only slightly, to 6.6 hours and then 6.9 hours, so that in the oldest group men sleep around 20 minutes longer than women.

tasks.title: Positive or negative development essay: international tourism
tasks.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

International tourism has grown enormously in recent decades, and many places now receive millions of foreign visitors every year.

Is this a positive or negative development for the countries that tourists visit?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
tasks.modelAnswer:
Cheap flights, rising incomes and the internet have made foreign travel possible for millions of people who could never have afforded it in the past. As a result, many countries now depend heavily on international visitors. In my opinion, this growth is largely positive for host countries, although it creates problems that need careful management.

The main benefit is economic. Tourists spend money on hotels, restaurants, transport and souvenirs, creating jobs for local people, including many who might otherwise have few opportunities, such as those living in rural areas. The taxes generated by tourism can pay for roads, airports and public services that benefit residents as well as visitors. In addition, tourism can help to protect cultural heritage and nature, because historic buildings and national parks become valuable sources of income that governments have reasons to preserve.

Tourism can also bring cultural benefits. When visitors meet local people, both sides can learn about different ways of life, which may reduce prejudice and increase understanding between nations.

However, mass tourism also has negative effects. In popular cities, such as some in southern Europe, the large number of short-term rentals for tourists has pushed up rents, forcing local residents out of the city centre. Crowds can damage fragile sites, and the waste and pollution produced by tourists harm the environment. There is also a risk that local traditions become performances for visitors rather than part of real life.

Nevertheless, these problems can be reduced through sensible policies, such as limiting visitor numbers at sensitive sites, regulating holiday rentals and investing tourist taxes in local communities.

In conclusion, I believe that the growth of international tourism is a positive development overall, as long as host countries control it so that local people share its benefits.
